title: The power that puts speech together: one voice, and Abba who founded the daughter
overview:
Chapter 50 takes the five *gevuros* of *MNTzPCh* down into speech. They are the five places of the mouth, throat, lips, palate, tongue and teeth, and they cut the one breath of the voice into letters. *Sefer Yetzira* says He calls each letter by name and makes it king: the way a computer calls letters onto a screen, and the way the brain does in every word, which is why a little baby cannot talk well yet.

But one voice connects all the combinations, like the thread through the beads of a necklace: the general thought of the whole idea, rooted in *chachma*. Lose it and a person says "ah", his face goes blank, and he reaches up for a moment of bewilderment before he can talk again. So the *koach hamatzref*, the power that puts speech together, is from *chachma*, *Abba yasad b'rata*: a child talks with no preparation. That power is what makes man *medaber*, the speaking soul. The chapter's last eleven lines, on the six days and Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, have no recording.

sections.title: The five places of the mouth: the gevuros that give each letter its place
sections.summary: The five *gevuros* of *MNTzPCh* in speech are the five places of the mouth (throat, lips, palate, tongue and teeth), each with letters of its own.

phrases.he: (נ) והנה ידוע בפרטות ענין ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך שבדבור די' מאמרות דאימא אוזיפת כו', שהן ה' מוצאות הפה
אחה"ע מהגרון
וגיכ"ק מהחיך כו',
הרי יש אותיות מיוחדים לכל מוצא בפני עצמו

blocks.text: The five *gevuros* (powers of restraint) of *MNTzPCh* in speech are the five *motza'os hapeh* (places of articulation), all from *Sefer Yetzira*. *Alef, ches, hei, ayin*: the throat. *Beis, vav, mem, pei*: the lips. *Gimmel, yud, kaf, kuf*: the *cheich*, the palate. *Dalet, tes, lamed, nun, tof*: the tongue. *Zayin, samech, shin, reish, tzadi*: the teeth, the *reish* being the tongue on the teeth.

sections.title: Calling up the letters: how the combinations are made
sections.summary: The letters combine as *Sefer Yetzira* says: one letter is called up and made king, then goes back for the next, as a computer calls letters onto a screen and as the brain does in every word a person says.

phrases.he: והצירופים נמצאים בחיבור והתכללות מזה לזה בכמה אופנים שונים
וכמו שכתוב בספר יצירה וקבען בפה כו'
phrases.en: He *kovea* the letters with a name.

phrases.he: המליך אות כו'
phrases.en: He took a letter and made it the king: the king of the *dibur*.

phrases.he: עד צא וחשוב כי מה' אותיות נעשה ק"ך צירופים כו'

blocks.text: The letters are joined in many ways, as *Sefer Yetzira* says. **He *kovea* the letters with a name**: He calls them, as in spelling: now, *alef*, come up.

blocks.title: The letters called up like a computer
blocks.text: Take the first word of this chapter: *vav*, come up; now go back, and *hei*, come up; then *nun*, then *hei*. That is how a computer calls letters onto the screen, and how a person talks: he thinks in whole words, but his brain calls up each letter. Without this computer thing of *bina* (understanding), separating the idea into letters, he could not talk.
It is already second nature, like riding a bicycle. A baby who knows the words still cannot talk well, because he has not got the mechanism of calling up the letters.
*Himlich os*: **He took a letter and made it the king: the king of the *dibur*** (speech). By the way, five letters make 120 *tzirufim* (combinations), the 120 combinations of the Name *Elokim*.

sections.title: One voice holds all the combinations together
sections.summary: The *gevuros* divide the breath of the voice into combinations, but one voice, rooted in *chachma*, connects them all, as a thread holds the beads of a necklace. When a person loses that general thought he says "ah" and cannot talk.

phrases.he: והן על ידי בחינת ה׳ גבורות המפרידות הבל הדבור
phrases.en: That's through the five *gevuros*, which is the *motza'os hapeh*, which separates.

phrases.he: כי יש בדבור חומר וצורה, הבל קול הדבור, חומר המורכב מאש מים ורוח,
והקול מתחלק בצירופים שונים,
phrases.en: The *kol* has to be divided up in the mouth into the different *tzirufim*.

phrases.he: ואמנם קול אחד הוא המחבר לכללות כל הצירופים יחד
phrases.en: Nonetheless it's one voice that connects all the *tzirufim* together.

blocks.text: Combinations come **through the five *gevuros*, which is the *motza'os hapeh*, which separates**. Talking needs a breath, an "ah"; people who lost their voice box put a funny little thing on their throat. Here the tape side ends.

The next side picks it up. Talking starts with an "ah", an *alef*, out of the lungs: so *Malchus* (kingship) comes out of *Zeir Anpin*, undifferentiated. The *gevuros*, *davka* (specifically) in *Malchus*, differentiate, and have a higher source than the voice: the voice carries the emotion, but its exact detail comes from the *gevuros* of *Malchus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 229 opens by finishing the explanation of line 5 that the end of class 228 broke off, before it reads line 6.

blocks.text: Speech has *chomer* (matter) and form. The *chomer* is the breath of the voice, from *Zeir Anpin*; then **the *kol* has to be divided up in the mouth into the different *tzirufim***, and yet **it's one voice that connects all the *tzirufim* together**.

blocks.question: I thought the voice only has the emotion. How can it be what connects the combinations?
blocks.text: The voice has a higher root too, in *chachma* (wisdom): besides the emotion, it holds the connection.

blocks.title: The "ah" of a lost train of thought
blocks.text: So a person who loses the connection goes "ah, ah", with no emotion, only a question mark: what did I want to say? He scratches his head, eyes going up. Head and eyes down are a sign of *daas* (knowledge), as the saying goes; up, of trying to remember, reaching back to the flash of *chachma*, the *nekuda* (point) of the whole idea. He lost his train of thought.

So the whole idea is in the voice, and with it the *kala d'mishtama* (the voice that is heard): the emotion, sad or happy, a victory, or a *hoda'a* (acknowledgement) like "Wow!" at something's splendor. Emotion comes from *chachma*, the overview of the whole situation, not from separate letters. The voice in speech calls the idea down from the essence: that is the "uh".

It says in places that *chachma* is a question and *bina* an answer: *koach MaH*, the power of "what". That is the "uh", the cartoons' "er". He is thinking, but not in letters of thought; with those he would have letters of speech. He lost them, and is reaching up to the *koach hamaskil* (the power that brings insight).

blocks.question: It says *bina* is *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna*, and *chachma* is *chachma* and *bina*. Isn't *chachma* *chachma* and *Yisroel Saba*, and *bina* *bina* and *tevuna*?
blocks.text: Losing the train of thought is losing *bina*, and revealed *chachma*, the outside of *chachma*, is part of *bina*: neither exists without the other. So he must go back to the idea in its *hiyuli* (formless) state, their source in *Arich*, and bring it out into a *yesh* (something). That "uh" is the *koach MaH* of *chachma* going up to see what he was saying.

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין צווארך בחרוזים,
phrases.en: You have pearls on your throat.

phrases.he: כמו חוט שבחרוזים של כמה אבנים שמחברם יחד
phrases.en: Like a thread that goes through the *charuzim*, the beads or pearls, and connects them together into a necklace.

blocks.title: The thread through the beads
blocks.text: As explained elsewhere on "your neck with strings of beads": **you have pearls on your throat**. The thread of thought is **like a thread that goes through the *charuzim*, the beads or pearls, and connects them together into a necklace**.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בבחינת אותיות מחשבה שבדבור, שיש מחשבה כללית המקפת ומחברת כל פרטי אותיות המחשבה שבכל פרטי הדבורים
וכך הוא בקול שבמחשבה עצמה מה׳ גבורות דאימא כו')

blocks.text: While letters come out, a person must think the whole idea at once, or he cannot talk; even "get me the screwdriver" needs the whole of what he wants in his head. That is the *machshava klalis hamakefes* (the surrounding general thought).
Without it he cannot talk. In thought too, letters the general thought does not hold get mixed up: he cannot contain the thought.
Someone says you're mixing him up. "What are you, an egg or something?" It really means the letters are getting mixed up in his brain.

sections.title: The power that combines comes from chachma
sections.summary: The details of the combinations come from *bina*, but the power that puts them together comes by itself from the *koach MaH* of *chachma*: a child talks with no preparation, and a person who has lost his thought is bewildered for a moment and then can talk again.

phrases.he: והנה ידוע דאבא יסד ברתא, כמו שכתוב מצרף לחכמה כו'
והיינו על דרך הנזכר לעיל במחשבה, שגוף הצירופים בדבור הוא רק על ידי בחינת ה׳ גבורות המצמצם אופן השכל שבדבור,
שעל פי זה דווקא יומשכו אופן הצירופים
ועל כן כפי הוראת המכוון במחשבה שבדבור, כך יהיה דוקא אופני הצירופים משתנים בכל עת כו'
phrases.en: So according to what he's thinking, the *machshava* of the *dibur*, the general *machshava*: according to that will be the *tzirufim* of the talk.

phrases.he: והיינו מאמר דאימא דוקא אוזיפת כו', שהוא בחינת בינה, אימא עילאה שנמשך באימא תתאה, בחינת בינה שמלובש במחשבה שבדבור, שהוא בפרט אופן כל צירוף שבדבור כו'

blocks.text: It is known that *Abba yasad b'rata* (the father founded the daughter). The five *gevuros* contract the intellect into speech's combinations, so **according to what he's thinking, the *machshava* of the *dibur***, his general thought, will be the combinations of the talk.
This is the saying about *Ima*: *bina*, the upper *Ima*, drawn into the *Ima tata'a* (the lower mother), here meaning speech, the way of each combination.

phrases.he: אך מה שכתוב מצרף לחכמה, היינו שרש כח המצרף לצרופים הללו שעל פי השכל דבינה
שהרי אנו רואים שמיד שירצה לדבר בדרך אופן צירופים פרטים, איננו צריך לעיין בשכל והשגה דבינה איך לצרף, שהרי התינוק שמדבר יודע מיד לצרף הדבור, בלתי צריך הכנה לזה כלל
כי שרש כח המצרף הזה ממילא בא, מצד הארת כח מ"ה דחכמה שלמעלה מהשגה דבינה, והיינו מבחינת כח המשכיל עצמו, מקור החכמה כו'

blocks.text: Combining is from *chachma*, the root of the *koach hamatzref* (the power that combines). A child who talks knows at once how to put speech together. A person does no analysis: he thinks about the *inyan* (matter), not how to cut it up, and it happens automatically, because he is thinking about the source of the *bina*.

It sounds like backward logic. *Tziruf* means putting together, the opposite of *chiluk* (division), yet he says the voice is divided into various *tzirufim*, not various divisions. He keeps saying every combination in speech comes from *bina*, then says *metzaref l'chachma*: the combining is *davka* in *chachma*. The point: *tziruf* means putting it together, not taking it apart.

A person who talks thinks not how to take it apart, nor even how to put it together, but how it is already together: the *koach MaH* of *chachma*, *batel* (nullified) to the *inyan*. Saying "ah", he is *batel* to it for a minute, and then can talk again.

blocks.title: The blank look when a person stops to think
blocks.text: For that minute he does not know how to talk. Look at a person when he says "ah": his face goes blank, sort of, his eyes go up a little or wander from side to side, sometimes his mouth opens, and a weird, confused expression comes on his face, like a crazy person's. He does not look crazy only because it lasts a second and people are used to it; a crazy person stays like that. When a person stops to think, it happens so fast that people do not notice.

sensitivity.reason: Uses "a crazy person", someone mentally ill, as the picture of the blank look of a person who stops to think.
sensitivity.publishable: For that minute he does not know how to talk. Look at a person when he says "ah": his face goes blank, sort of, his eyes go up a little or wander from side to side, sometimes his mouth opens, and a weird, confused expression comes on his face. It lasts a second and people are used to it. When a person stops to think, it happens so fast that people do not notice.

blocks.text: He thinks 5668 explains that before the actual idea comes there is *timahon*: between confusion and wonderment; a listener finds the word, bewilderment. That bewilderment is the *koach MaH* of *chachma*: he does not know, he is without an explanation, seeing the whole concept at one shot without letters. Then he brings it back down, and all of a sudden he can talk again.

So he need not analyze with *bina* how to combine; his "ah" is not working out what to say. A child combines speech at once, unprepared: the combining power comes by itself from the *koach MaH* of *chachma*, the *koach hamaskil* itself.

sections.title: The speaking soul: speech comes from Abba
sections.summary: Speech comes from *Abba*, from the soul itself: the power that puts speech together is what makes man *medaber*, a speaker, and is not the wisdom inside the utterances.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ויהי האדם לנפש חיה, שהוא פנימיות קדמות החכמה, אז יוכל לדבר ונקרא רוחא ממללא כו')
והיינו המאמר דאבא יסד ברתא כידוע
phrases.en: That means that the speech really comes from *Abba*, not from *Ima*.

blocks.text: As explained elsewhere on "and man became a living soul": with the inside of *chachma* he can talk, and is called *ruach memalela* (the speaking spirit). This is *Abba yasad b'rata*: **that means that the speech really comes from *Abba*, not from *Ima***.

phrases.he: (ומה שאמר בראשית נמי מאמר הוא,
phrases.en: This thing it says, *Bereishis* is also a *maamar*

phrases.he: קאי על חכמה ושכל שבמאמרות,
phrases.en: That's talking about the actual *chachma* which is in the *maamarim* themselves.

phrases.he: ולא על כח המצרף,
שזהו בכללות כל מדבר שנקרא נפש המדברת כו')
phrases.en: That's the actual talker: not the *maamar*, the *omer*, the one who's speaking.

blocks.text: That ***Bereishis* is also a *maamar*** (an utterance) is not about this. **That's talking about the actual *chachma* which is in the *maamarim* themselves**, not the *koach hamatzref* that every speaker has, the *nefesh hamedaberes* (speaking soul): the *omer*, the one speaking, not the *maamar*.

phrases.he: והוא עיקר בחינת אדם שנקרא מדבר,
phrases.en: That's the main *inyan* of what *adam* is, which is called *medaber*.

phrases.he: דהיינו כח ומקור הצירוף של הדבור,
phrases.en: The *koach* and *makor* of the putting together of the *dibur*, not the splitting apart.

phrases.he: כמו שנקרא נפש המדברת דוקא כו'
phrases.en: The *nefesh* is called *medaberes davka*: not thinking.

phrases.he: (והיינו כאשר מבחינת שרש ומקור האותיות שבנפש עצמה,
phrases.en: Really it's according to the *osios* in the *nefesh* itself.

phrases.he: שבאין לידי גלוי בבחינת דבור שבנפש עצמו,
phrases.en: The *dibur* comes from the *nefesh* itself. The *nefesh* is talking.

phrases.he: כשנקרא נפש המדברת רוח ממללא כו')

blocks.text: This is the main *inyan* of what *adam* (man) is, called *medaber* (a speaker): **the *koach* and *makor* of the putting together of the *dibur*, not the splitting apart**. Speaking *davka*, not thinking: not homo sapiens but "homo blabians, I guess, talking man."

It goes by the *osios* (letters) in the soul itself, above intellect, even above *ratzon* (will) and *taanug* (delight): **The *dibur* comes from the *nefesh* itself. The *nefesh* is talking.** Hence *nefesh hamedaberes*, *ruach memalela*.

sections.title: The combinations of the six days, and the tzaddik who changes them (not recorded)
sections.summary: By the chapter's text: the combinations change through the six days of the *middos* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, from *chesed* to *din*, and a *tzaddik* like Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, who said that vinegar should burn, rules through the 120 combinations of *Elokim*. No class of the series reads these lines.

skip.note: No class in the series reads this line: class 229 stops at line 21, and the next class in the catalog (230, tape 57) is on chapter 52; tape 56 is not in the catalog.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the five places of the mouth, and which letters come from each?
How is talking like a computer calling letters up onto a screen, and why can a little baby not talk well even when he knows the words?
If the voice is divided into combinations in the mouth, what connects them, and what does a person's "ah" show about it?
Why does even "get me the screwdriver" need a general thought, and what happens to the letters without one?
Why does calling the combinations tzirufim sound like backward logic, and what does the bewilderment before an idea teach about where the power that combines comes from?
Why is man called medaber, and why is that not what "Bereishis is also a maamar" refers to?

A reminder of the combinations and the general thought, the train of thought, that connects them.
"I'm going to stop here because they're already..."; the tape ends.

notes.text: Lines 22-32 have no recording. Class 229 (tape 55, side 2) stops after line 21 ("I'm going to stop here"), and the next class in the catalog, 230, is tape 57 on chapter 52: tape 56, which would have finished chapter 50 and taught chapter 51, is not in the catalog. The title and summary of section 6 paraphrase the chapter text, not a class.

Line 2: he first reads the palate group as nun, yud, kaf, kuf and corrects it to gimmel from the book. The transcript gives the teeth group as zayin, shin, shin, reish, tzadi; the block writes samech for the first shin, as the group is in Sefer Yetzira and as he means five letters.

Line 4: he reads "ויקבעם בשם" (set them by name) where the line has "וקבען בפה" (set them in the mouth), and his English ("He kovea the letters with a name") and the computer mashal follow his reading. He also seems to read "אז דרך אגב" ("so, by the way") where the line has "עד צא וחשוב"; the block keeps "by the way". The last phrase of the line ("from five letters 120 combinations") has no English: he only adds that they are the 120 combinations of Elokim.

Class 228 ends in the middle of the explanation of line 5 (people who lost their voice box), and class 229 opens by finishing it before it reads line 6; lines 5 and 6 are one sentence of the text, so they are one passage, and the opening of 229 is marked outOfPlace.

229 w398-426: the transcript has "what the רבה said" for the source of the saying about head and eyes going down (daas) or up (remembering); probably "the Rebbe", but which Rebbe (or whether it is Rabba) is not clear, so the block says only "as the saying goes".

229 w861-1080: the question about chachma being chachma and bina and bina being Yisroel Saba and tevuna is his own; the transcript's wording is muddled ("it says that bina is Yisroel Saba and tevuna, and it says that chachma is chachma and bina"), and the block keeps it as he says it.

229 w2342-2411: he says "I think in תרס"ח" (5668) for where timahon is explained; the block keeps his "I think". The word "bewilderment" seems to come from a listener and he takes it up; inferred from the exchange.

Lines 10-11, 13-17: read without English; the phrases are Hebrew only. Line 13 he reads "דאזלת לזיפה" for "אוזיפת" and glosses only that Ima tata'a here means speech. Line 17 he reads "פנימיות עצמות החכמה" where the line has "פנימיות קדמות החכמה".

The "crazy person" mashal (229 w2016-2338) is flagged as a simile drawn from the mentally ill; it is the image of his point, not a teaching about them, so the public text drops only the comparison, and the reviewer decides whether it needs softening at all (recommend judgment).
229 w1065-1080: after the chachma/bina question he returns to line 6 ("one voice connects all the combinations") before reading line 7; folded into the question block's stretch, not written out.
